To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have calculated the masses of bottomonium states and found good agreement with experiment, and that we have determined the parameters of a nonperturbatively improved relativistic heavy quark action that can be used in future calculations of B-meson matrix elements.

we have developed a method to tune the parameters of the clover-improved relativistic heavy-quarks action nonperturbative such that it reproduces the experimental values of bottomonium states, and have used this method to calculate the masses of the bottomonium states with total uncertainties of 0.5- 0.6%.

the relativistic heavy quark action is a good approximation to the full QCD Lagrangian, that it is possible to tune the three parameters nonperturbatively to reproduce the experimental values for the B_s and its excited states, that this tuning can be done without any additional inputs, that it is then possible to compute the bottomonium spectrum with no additional inputs and that the results are in good agreement with experiment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of hadrons containing heavy quarks.
the calculation of hadronic properties using lattice gauge theory methods.

the calculation of the masses of bottom and bottomonium hadrons using a relativistic heavy-quarks action that is nonperturbatively tuned to reproduce the experimental values for the B_s and the B_s* states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have a reliable method to calculate the spectrum of heavy-light mesons and bottomonium, and we have demonstrated the reliability of our method by obtaining results for bottomonium masses and splittings that agree with experiment to within the statistical and systematic uncertainties.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and validated a method that is capable of computing heavy-light and heavy-heavy meson masses and decay constants with uncertainties that are of the size of the light pseudoscalar sector, which is the ultimate goal of lattice QCD calculations.
the nonperturbative tuning procedure for the relativistic heavy quark action is a powerful method to obtain precise results for heavy-light systems.

we have developed an improved heavy-quark action which has a small mass-independent error, and we have tuned the action nonpertubatively to obtain accurate predictions for heavy meson and heavyonium masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relativistic heavy quark action can be tuned to reproduce the experimental spectrum of heavy-light mesons, and the parameters of the action can be used for calculations of heavy-quark weak matrix elements with lattice discretization effects that are comparable in size to those in light pseudoscalars.

, with a judicious choice of the parameters of a relativistic heavy-quarks action, the systematic uncertainties in the calculation of heavy-light and heavy-heavy meson masses can be reduced to the level of a few percent.
, for the first time, we are able to calculate the masses of heavy-light mesons with uncertainties that are of the order of 1% using a nonperturbative tuning.
